## The path from a missed due date to one alert in one inbox

**What starts the check.** Nothing inside a request triggers this — it's driven externally. In-process, `src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts` runs an interval `tick()` every 60s and, per `CADENCE_MINUTES["overdue-issues"] = 60`, enqueues an `overdue-issues` job about once an hour; `src/server/jobs/queue.ts`'s `drain()`/`runHandler` dynamically dispatches it. The same work can also be triggered externally: `POST /api/cron/overdue` (`src/app/api/cron/overdue/route.ts`) is a thin trigger that calls `assertCronSecret(request)` (a shared-secret header check, since the platform scheduler has no session cookie) and then calls `runOverdueIssueJob(new Date())` from `src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts`. Either path lands on the same function, and the route comment notes calling it twice in the same window is harmless — the job itself is what makes repeated triggers safe.

**Narrowing the set of issues that count.** `runOverdueIssueJob` (wrapped in `runJob` for the `JobResult` accounting) first checks `shouldFilterArchived(LIVE_ONLY)` as a sanity guard, then calls `usageRepo.listOrgIdsForRollup(ORG_BATCH)` to sweep organizations in batches of 50. For each org it calls `issueRepo.listOverdueIssues(orgId, stamp)` (`src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts`), which is where the real filtering happens: same org, not archived (`livePredicate`), `dueAt` not null, `dueAt < now`, and `status` still in `["backlog", "todo", "in_progress", "in_review"]` — i.e. closed or archived issues drop out of consideration entirely, which is also why an issue archived or marked done after going overdue is never reported.

**What the checking component does and doesn't own.** For each overdue issue not already seen (see dedup below), the job calls `emit("issue.overdue", {...})` from `@/lib/event-bus` with the issue id, project id, due date and assignee id — nothing more. That's the entire responsibility boundary: the job "announces the fact" and owns none of the notification logic (per its own header comment). It doesn't know or care who gets told, whether that's email or in-app, or whether the assignee even exists — it emits unconditionally and lets subscribers decide. Each emit is wrapped in try/catch: a failure just increments `result.failed` and logs via `createLogger("overdue-issue-job")`, so one bad issue doesn't stop the sweep for the rest. This is reinforced by the event bus itself (`src/lib/event-bus.ts`): handlers are isolated, so a throwing subscriber never fails the emit or other subscribers.

**What stops repeat announcements.** The job keeps a module-scope `reported = new Set<string>()` of issue ids "announced this process's lifetime." Before emitting it checks `reported.has(issue.id)` and skips; after a successful emit it adds the id. So the next hourly sweep still finds the same still-open, still-overdue issue via `listOverdueIssues`, but the `reported` check is what prevents a second `issue.overdue` emission for it. (`resetOverdueTracking()` exists only to clear this between test scenarios.)

**Fan-out and channel selection.** `src/server/services/notification-service.ts` calls `registerFanOut()` once at module load, subscribing to `"issue.overdue"`. Its handler is where the recipient is actually chosen: `if (payload.assigneeId === null) return` — an unassigned overdue issue is emitted by the job but silently dropped here, since there's no one to tell. Otherwise it calls `notify(orgId, "issue_overdue", [assigneeId], {...})`. Inside `notify`, for that recipient it loads their `NotificationPreference` via `preferenceRepo.getPreference` and runs `resolveChannels(preference, flags)`: with no stored preference it defaults to `["in_app", "email"]`; otherwise `in_app` is included if `preference.inApp`, and `email` is included if `preference.email` and (not `digestOnly`, or the org's `digest_email` plan flag is on via `isEnabled`). If the resolved channel list is empty, the recipient is skipped entirely — no row is written for someone who muted everything. Otherwise `notificationRepo.insertNotifications` writes one `Notification` row carrying that `channels` array.

**How it reaches the person, per channel.** The `in_app` channel is realized simply by that row existing — the assignee's client (the notification store in `src/hooks/notification-store.ts`, backed by `listNotifications`/`countUnread` in the same service) picks it up as soon as it queries again, so delivery is effectively immediate. The `email` channel is *not* sent synchronously by `notify()` — `insertNotifications` (`src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts`) only persists the row. Actual email transmission happens later, out-of-band, in `runDigestEmailJob` (`src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts`), which runs on its own hourly tick but only acts for an org during its configured `digestHourUtc` (`shouldRunForOrg`), and only for recipients who are digest subscribers (`listDigestRecipients` → `preferenceRepo.listDigestSubscribers`). For each such recipient, `buildDigest` (`src/server/services/digest-service.ts`) gathers their still-unread notifications from the last day (including the `issue_overdue` row), `renderDigest` renders one combined "digest" email, and `sendEmail` (`src/server/services/email-service.ts`, which in this codebase just logs the draft rather than doing real network egress) delivers it. The job then calls `notificationRepo.markRead` on every bundled entry — which is what prevents the same overdue issue from being emailed again in tomorrow's digest window. Note there's a dedicated `overdue-email.tsx` / `"overdue"` template in `src/emails/`, described as "produced by the overdue job," but nothing in the job or fan-out actually renders or sends it — it's exercised only by the template smoke test (`tests/emails/render.test.ts`); the real email a user gets is the generic digest, not this template.

So end to end: scheduler/cron → `runOverdueIssueJob` narrows to live, still-open, past-due issues per org → emits `issue.overdue` once per issue thanks to the in-memory `reported` set → `notification-service`'s fan-out drops unassigned issues and otherwise resolves the assignee's chosen channels → one `Notification` row is written → in-app shows up immediately, email (if chosen) goes out once via the next digest run for that recipient's org.
